### Page note: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21544-schizoaffective-disorder
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page:** What Is Schizoaffective Disorder? – https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21544-schizoaffective-disorder  

**Evidence**  
- Medications & therapies are part of schizoaffective treatment (combination of “therapy and medications”).  
- **Medications**  
  - *Antipsychotics*: “primary type of medicine used to treat the symptoms that resemble schizophrenia — delusions, hallucinations and disordered thinking.”  
  - *Mood stabilizers*: “primary type of medicine used to treat and prevent mania. Lithium and valproate are examples of mood stabilizers.”  
  - *Antidepressants*: “primary type of medicine used to treat and prevent depression. Fluoxetine and sertraline are examples of antidepressants.”  
- **Psychotherapy**  
  - “Psychotherapy is a form of talk therapy … the goal of psychotherapy is to learn about the condition, establish personal goals, and manage everyday challenges.”  
  - *Family therapy* is listed as another type of psychotherapy.  
- **Skills training** (a form of counseling): “often focuses on day‑to‑day activities, grooming and hygiene, social skills, work or school responsibilities.”  
- The page is medically reviewed and “Last updated on 10/03/2023.”  

**Coverage**  
- The page covers **treatment methods for schizoaffective disorder only** (medications and psychotherapy, plus skills training).  
- It does **not** provide any information on schizophrenia treatments or refer to Mayo Clinic.  
- The listed treatment methods appear to be a complete set presented on the page (no truncated tables).  

**Missing**  
- Treatment methods for **schizophrenia** (from Cleveland Clinic).  
- Any **mention of Mayo Clinic** treatment methods.  
- Confirmation that these methods are also present in Mayo Clinic as of July 2025.  

**Next links**  
- https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/4568-schizophrenia – Cleveland Clinic’s schizophrenia page (likely contains schizophrenia treatments).  
- https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/schizoaffective-disorder/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20356226 – Mayo Clinic page for schizoaffective disorder (may list treatments).  
- https://www.mayoclinic.org/diagnosis-tests/schizophrenia/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20356214 – Mayo Clinic page for schizophrenia (may list treatments).

### Page note: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/4568-schizophrenia

- *Management and Treatment* section describes the following treatment methods for schizophrenia:  
  - **Medications:** “several types of antipsychotics can help manage symptoms.”  
  - **Psychotherapy:** “talk therapy, like cognitive behavioral therapy (CBTp) for psychosis.”  
  - **Supportive services:** “resilience training, family therapy, cognitive support, and help with work or school.”  
  - **Other options if medications don’t improve symptoms:** “electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).”

  - Brexpiprazole (Rexulti®)  
  - Cariprazine (Vraylar®)  
  - Clozapine (Clozaril®)  
  - Haloperidol (Haldol®)  
  - Lurasidone (Latuda®)  
  - Lumateperone (Caplyta®)  
  - Olanzapine (Zyprexa®, Lybalvi®, Symbyax®)  
  - Quetiapine (Seroquel®)  
  - Risperidone (Risperdal®, Perseris®, Risperdal Consta®)  
  - Xanomeline and trospium (Cobenfy™)

**Coverage**  
- Entity: Schizophrenia (diagnosis: mental health disorder).  
- Treatment methods covered: Medications (antipsychotics), Psychotherapy (CBTp and general talk therapy), Supportive services, Electroconvulsive therapy.

**Evidence**  
*Treatment Methods for Schizophrenia*  

| Category | Treatment Method | Note | Source Quote |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicines | Antipsychotic medicines | Main pharmacologic treatment | “Medicines are the main schizophrenia treatment.” |
|  | • Second‑generation antipsychotics: Aripiprazole (Abilify), Asenapine (Saphris), Brexpiprazole (Rexulti), Cariprazine (Vraylar), Clozapine (Clozaril), Iloperidone (Fanapt), Lumateperone (Caplyta), Lurasidone (Latuda), Olanzapine (Zyprexa), Paliperidone (Invega), Quetiapine (Seroquel), Risperidone (Risperdal), Xanomeline and trospium chloride (Cobenfy), Ziprasidone (Geodon) | “The newer, second‑generation medicines available as a pill or capsule include: …” | “The newer, second‑generation medicines available as a pill or capsule include:” |
|  | • First‑generation antipsychotics: Chlorpromazine, Fluphenazine, Haloperidol (Haldol), Perphenazine (Trilafon) | “First‑generation antipsychotics include: …” | “First‑generation antipsychotics include:” |
|  | • Long‑acting injectable antipsychotics: Aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), Fluphenazine decanoate, Haloperidol decanoate, Paliperidone (Invega Sustenna, Invega Trinza, Invega Hafyera), Risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, others) | “Common medicines that are available as shots include: …” | “Common medicines that are available as shots include:” |
|  | • Other medicines: Antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antianxiety drugs | “Other medicines also may help, such as antidepressants, mood stabilizers or antianxiety drugs.” | “Other medicines also may help, such as antidepressants, mood stabilizers or antianxiety drugs.” |

|  | Social skills training | “Social skills training focuses on ...” | “Social skills training focuses on …” |
|  | Family therapy | “During this therapy, families learn how to deal with schizophrenia.” | “During this therapy, families learn how to deal with schizophrenia.” |
|  | Vocational rehabilitation and supported employment | “This counseling focuses on helping people with schizophrenia prepare for, find and keep jobs.” | “Vocational rehabilitation and supported employment. This counseling focuses on helping people with schizophrenia prepare for, find and keep jobs.” |
|  | Hospital stay | “During crisis periods or times of severe symptoms, people may need to stay in a hospital.” | “During crisis periods or times of severe symptoms, people may need to stay in a hospital for their safety.” |

*Treatment Methods for Schizophrenia*  

| Category | Treatment Method | Note | Source Quote |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicines | Antipsychotic medicines | Main pharmacologic treatment | “Medicines are the main schizophrenia treatment.” |
|  | • Second‑generation antipsychotics: Aripiprazole (Abilify), Asenapine (Saphris), Brexpiprazole (Rexulti), Cariprazine (Vraylar), Clozapine (Clozaril), Iloperidone (Fanapt), Lumateperone (Caplyta), Lurasidone (Latuda), Olanzapine (Zyprexa), Paliperidone (Invega), Quetiapine (Seroquel), Risperidone (Risperdal), Xanomeline and trospium chloride (Cobenfy), Ziprasidone (Geodon) | “The newer, second‑generation medicines available as a pill or capsule include: …” | “The newer, second‑generation medicines available as a pill or capsule include:” |
|  | • First‑generation antipsychotics: Chlorpromazine, Fluphenazine, Haloperidol (Haldol), Perphenazine (Trilafon) | “First‑generation antipsychotics include: …” | “First‑generation antipsychotics include:” |
|  | • Long‑acting injectable antipsychotics: Aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), Fluphenazine decanoate, Haloperidol decanoate, Paliperidone (Invega Sustenna, Invega Trinza, Invega Hafyera), Risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, others) | “Common medicines that are available as shots include: …” | “Common medicines that are available as shots include:” |
|  | • Other medicines: Antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antianxiety drugs | “Other medicines also may help, such as antidepressants, mood stabilizers or antianxiety drugs.” | “Other medicines also may help, such as antidepressants, mood stabilizers or antianxiety drugs.” |
| Psychosocial Interventions | Individual therapy (talk therapy / psychotherapy) | “Talk therapy, also known as psychotherapy, may help improve patterns of thought.” | “Talk therapy, also known as psychotherapy, may help improve patterns of thought.” |
|  | Social skills training | “Social skills training focuses on ...” | “Social skills training focuses on …” |
|  | Family therapy | “During this therapy, families learn how to deal with schizophrenia.” | “During this therapy, families learn how to deal with schizophrenia.” |
|  | Vocational rehabilitation and supported employment | “This counseling focuses on helping people with schizophrenia prepare for, find and keep jobs.” | “Vocational rehabilitation and supported employment. This counseling focuses on helping people with schizophrenia prepare for, find and keep jobs.” |
|  | Hospital stay | “During crisis periods or times of severe symptoms, people may need to stay in a hospital.” | “During crisis periods or times of severe symptoms, people may need to stay in a hospital for their safety.” |
|  | Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) | “Healthcare professionals may consider ECT for adults with schizophrenia who don’t respond to drug therapy.” | “Healthcare professionals may consider electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for adults with schizophrenia who don’t respond to drug therapy.” |
